subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For Codex-backed turns interrupted by Gateway restart or app-server client close after possible side effects, should OpenClaw resume, synthesize a final status, or fail closed with restart-specific recovery guidance?
rationale: The current implementation has partial retry and restart-marker mechanisms, but the remaining behavior crosses replay safety, Codex transport failure classification, Gateway lifecycle, and channel delivery policy; automation cannot choose that product boundary safely.

options.title: Design restart-aware recovery
options.body: Define a cross-surface policy for Gateway-shutdown interruption, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused source and live proof.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics and copy
options.body: Keep runtime behavior fail-closed but make logs and channel copy distinguish Gateway restart from unexpected app-server failure.

options.title: Wait for live reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open under needs-live-repro until a current-main live run proves the remaining long-maintenance failure path and narrows the fix boundary.

recommendation.title: Design restart-aware recovery
recommendation.body: Define a cross-surface policy for Gateway-shutdown interruption, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused source and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current narrow Codex app-server recovery policy and user-facing copy trace to steipete's merged retry-boundary work, making them the best available owner for the product decision.
